author: Rdk123
text:
Hi all, apologies for the lack of posting! Like most of you I have a day job, I try and learn RTM on in the background and learn when I can but it's very sporadic.

I feel a lot of things have fallen in to place and when I have the time I will post demo trades and see what everyone thinks.

One thing I have been thinking about it is accuracy at which the masters trade. It does confirm that nothing in the market is 'random' to be able to do this.

I set myself the task this afternoon to look for a trade in the past that I may have taken using the knowledge from RTM. On top of that I wanted to find the real reason price turned at that exact point. Hopefully the charts below will show you what I have found.

My thought process was this;

1. Look for a trade at a flag limit. 2. remember the flag limit is itself a flag so look for the associated FTR. 3. Within the FTR look for the point at which the decision was made to turn price in the opposite direction, which I believe was an FTR in itself. 4. Price returned to the FTR, within the FTR of the FL. A mouth full but makes sense.

I'm going to find more of these examples but here is the first;

Any feedback is much appreciated.

author: Rdk123
text:
Evening all.

So, since Friday I have been able to think of nothing but that particular chart I posted. I felt I was so close to my own understanding of the price movements.

I also thought about a lot of other things when I remembered all of the hours I've put in staring at charts, reading journals and doing homework. To be honest I should have put more of it in my journal, I can't change that but I can carry on with the RTM ethos of teaching, not that I'm ready to teach yet but I honestly believe I will be.

I believe we can all have a different understanding of the same concept leading us to the same outcome. This is the benefit of putting our own jigsaw pieces together I suppose. If I just watched someone else put it together would I really understand or would I just be copying them and thinking 'shit, what do I do' when it has all gone wrong.

I was reading Warrens journal on Friday night. If you haven't done so, I recommend you do as it's an essential read. Know yourself and know who you are. He also has a Nissan GTR, a car my Dad loves and something I will hopefully purchase for him one day.

When I trade live I've decided I will only be doing so with a good foundation, at the base of that foundation will be good money management, knowing my loses will be limited to an amount I can psychologically deal with. This will give me great piece of mind which mean the amount I trade will not affect my judgement. The goal is to be a good trader, not to make money, if I'm a good trader the money will come as a byproduct. I liken this to any profession the best people in their field can demand the highest wages!

So, I've been going backwards and forwards a lot this week, a couple of phrases sticking in my mind. These aren't exact quotes but here I go ' the space between two FL's is a PAZ', 'I only trade FL's'. There are a few more but I might use them in another post!

I believe my journey has only just started, on Friday gone actually, everything before that was just preparation, putting talcum powder on my feet and stocking up on supplies. The following chart is a snippet of where I'm at, it is on the daily TF (I couldn't go down any further in the chart to draw some of the flag limits more accurately but I hope you get the concept of where I'm at).

All the best,

Robbie

Edit: I know there are more flag limits, but in this timeframe this is what I've drawn. Also, all targets are the next FL, I've not marked all FL's that could be targets. In my next post I'm going to look at when to exit a trade. ' There is no PA without an engulf' will be the basis of this, I would apply this to entries as well!

author: Rdk123
text:
Lots of thinking going on right now. Few more penny's dropping. Still lots of questions though.

This is where I'm at right now; I think if we engulf a FL/RBR/BDR we want to go to the next FL, this could be another DBD/RBR but we would be targeting the RBD/DBR within the DBD/RBR. Or we could be heading for the origin of the whole move down, we could just draw a box around the cap on price and make that our target, or we could look for the source, the FL/FTR, the real beginning of our move up or down.

I hope this makes sense. I'm just typing the things running around my head at the minute.

Where I am struggling when trying to prove this concept is in the lower time frames. I know it is irrelevant as long as we keep an eye on the bigger picture but it's knowing when to stop, knowing when to say, these are my targets, I know there are more FL's further down the time frames but these are the FL's I'm going to trade.

What importance do we put on an FTR that isn't a FL? The FTR to the FL has caught my attention so far. I from what I have seen a reaction should be expected there and it should be trade able as long as you look at the bigger picture.

People like to trade the same things in different ways. Dissecting IF's trades really helped me learn a lot, I hope I'm learning the correct things. IF seems to just go straight for the source as long as he has confirmation PA, and he then exits at the source of a move when he has confirmation that source will be the turning point for a move in the opposite direction. I think this is just part of IF's trading plan. Others look at the same area but take the trade after more confirmation.

That brings me nicely on to creating my own trading plan, how can I possibly think about becoming a trading without a plan.

1. Money management, the key. What am I willing to risk per trade? 2. What am I going to trade? Just FL's? FTR's? Only certain FTR's. Will I take multiple trades on the what I consider to be one move if I get additional confirmation PA that allows for another entry? 3. How many trades will I have open at any one time? 4. How many pairs/commodities will I monitor? I can't monitor them all, which ones will I chose? etc

What I've been looking for are basic rules, rules to follow the market, rules to put on top of my foundation of money management. If I have an engulf, I look for an entry. Looking at the charts this morning I'm realized I need more time in front of the charts to train myself and make this second nature, or close to.

I really believe price will go back to the source of a move if an engulf occurs, it's keeping an eye on what else has been engulfed.

Anyway, I've rambled far too much, I just had a lot of thoughts I needed to get out of my head. Hopefully at least one person can learn from my struggles, and if I might be heading in the wrong direction please just let me know.

author: Rdk123
text:
So, where I'm really struggling is defining my higher time frame supply and demand zones. In the homework area it's clear we could mark hundreds on one chart, but which ones are the important ones. I've read a lot about swing highs and swing lows, SR and FTRs.

When I look at the chart the swing highs and lows are just bouncing off flag limits, so by drawing my SR lines I am just marking of the boundries of the flags in the time frame I'm looking at. Then I have to remember that this high is bounching off something in the past, we know it's going to be a flag limit as this high is the limit of our flag. What i've done is mark the FTR after my highs around my SR lines, because this FTR is my flag limit.

Where I sometimes get unstuck is when my FTR after my high/low doesn't actually break the FL keeping the flag down/up. Do I ignore this FTR and give more importance to the FL/FTR which forms above? I'll have to look in to it more and see which gets respected.

Also, the SR Flip zone, this appears to be very strong, I know there will be a FL in the engulf somewhere but the SR flip zone appears to be an excellent place to look for longs/shorts

The following is my attempt and marking my HTF zones with the aim of being able to enter in the lower TF.
